title: [T1-d mint] Compose and persist the ApprovalDecisionRecord in approval.decide_intent, now that every roster fact resolves
description:
PARENT: task-f42d5165b747436a9f9b354dbfa37e3d (T1-c reader), which landed the tier's durable producer and thereby made this row reachable for the first time. Filed from the worker seat mid-step-4 because the remaining work needs THREE decisions a worker seat should not settle alone. NOT an evidence row: this is the production capability the T1 chain exists to reach.

MEASURED AT HEAD 076324e4 + task-f42d5165's delivered tree. `approval.decide_intent` now derives EVERY roster fact: riskTier (this parent, from the run's own PolicyEvaluated), stepUpAuthRef (task-3b61860f, from the composition-root witness), applicablePolicyRef (task-ba102165), budgetRef (task-be80cb74). `readApprovalRecordFacts` answers `ok: true` — verified by probe on the seam's own `reviewableStore()` fixture: `facts={"applicablePolicyRef":"e7a5ee19...","ok":true,"stepUpAuthRef":"e727c4ff..."}`. The production EDGE reaches the same point: `edgeRefusalOf(reviewableStore(), OPERATOR)` answers `APPROVAL_INTENT_RECORD_UNMINTED @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT`.

WHAT THE PARENT DID INSTEAD OF MINTING, and why this row must not undo it. `approval-intent.ts` previously ended with `burnStepUpAuthRef(...)` followed by `return refuse(null, APPROVAL_MISSING_FACT_CODES[3], LAYER)`, carrying a comment addressed to this row: *"making `facts.ok` reachable and leaving this refusal in place would BURN the one-shot reference and then refuse, bricking every retry."* Making `facts.ok` reachable is exactly what the parent did, so it inserted a guard ABOVE the burn returning the non-roster code `APPROVAL_INTENT_RECORD_UNMINTED`. The whole path is write-free today, and `approval-intent.test.ts`'s "burns NOTHING when the approval refuses" arm is now the anti-bricking regression guard.

DELIVER: delete THAT guard (not the terminal refusal), let the burn run as the last act before the record exists, compose the record, validate it through core's `validateApprovalRecord`, and commit exactly one durable ApprovalDecisionRecord event.

THE THREE DECISIONS THIS ROW NEEDS, each an authority question rather than an implementation detail:
1. DOES `approval.decide_intent` ALSO ACTIVATE? `planning-services.ts:224` documents `approval.decide` as "J1's approve-and-activate action" and its tail runs `verifyApprovedRunBinding` then the activation path. Minting a record without activating is a different product surface from the shipped one; activating is a materially larger authority act. Nothing in the T1 chain's plan text says which.
2. WHICH AGGREGATE AND EVENT TYPE holds the record, and how it relates to the record `approval.decide` commits from the caller's payload. Two durable records asserting one human approval is a supersession question.
3. THE TWO FIELDS WITH NO SERVER SOURCE. `validateApprovalRecord` (packages/core/src/policy/approval-validation.ts:24-29) demands 18 keys. Sixteen are available: five from `ApprovalIntentSources` (approvalRef, approvedNodeScope, criteriaRef, exactRevisionHash, planQualityAssessmentRef), four from `readApprovalRecordFacts`, two from the payload (decision, decisionReason), actor/actorKind/truthClass from the witness, policyDecisionRef null on the HUMAN branch, lifecycle "DECIDED". The remaining two — `validity` (a member of RUNTIME_LIFECYCLES.APPROVAL_VALIDITY) and `dependencyChanges` ({additions, challenges, removals}) — have NO durable producer and no derivation. Defaulting them would fabricate part of a HUMAN_APPROVED authority record, which is the precise thing epic rail 1 and the seam's own docstring forbid.

NOTE FOR PLANNING: `ApprovalRecordFactsComplete` currently returns only `{applicablePolicyRef, ok, stepUpAuthRef}` — the mint also needs `riskTier` and `budgetRef`, both already present in `derived`. Widening that interface is an owned edit for this row, not the parent's.

The three decisions in the description are ANSWERED BY AN ARCHITECT OR HUMAN before implementation, recorded on this row: (1) whether decide_intent activates, (2) the record's aggregate and event type and its relationship to approval.decide's payload-supplied record, (3) the producer or derivation for validity and dependencyChanges. A worker seat implementing any of the three by choosing a plausible value is a rejection.

The guard `return refuse(null, "APPROVAL_INTENT_RECORD_UNMINTED", LAYER)` is deleted in the SAME edit that lands the mint, so the burn becomes the last act before a record exists and never runs on a refusing path; an arm drives approval.decide_intent through the PRODUCTION command and asserts exactly one durable ApprovalDecisionRecord event, with the count asserted and the record re-read through core's validateApprovalRecord.

The anti-bricking property survives: an arm proves that any path which still refuses leaves the one-shot step-up reference unburned and re-burnable, asserting the exact code and layer of the refusal it drove.

Mutation drills with SHA256 restore proofs: move the burn above the mint -> the anti-bricking arm reds; drop one composed field -> validateApprovalRecord rejects and the mint arm reds naming that field. Gates standalone/unpiped with counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, the approval-intent/approval-record-facts suites from apps/daemon, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` path-attributed; every production source <= 250 lines; explicit-pathspec commit.
taskRails: Never default, derive or invent `validity` or `dependencyChanges` — both are parts of a HUMAN_APPROVED authority record and epic rail 1 says human authority is not delegable. Absent a named producer, report blocked.
Delete the parent's `APPROVAL_INTENT_RECORD_UNMINTED` guard only in the edit that lands the mint; never move the burn above a path that can still refuse.
Compose the existing readers — readApprovalIntentSources, readApprovalRecordFacts, deriveStepUpAuthRef. Never a second reader of the same durable bytes, never a caller-supplied record field.
Explicit-pathspec commits; foreign WIP preserved; <=250 lines per production source; TDD red-first through the production command.

comments.author: architect-fa5d746b
comments.content:
ARCHITECT RULINGS ON THE THREE DECISIONS (architect-fa5d746b, HEAD b14d0d77-era tree; DoD-2 names "ARCHITECT OR HUMAN" and these are architect-grade — a human may override any of the three on this surface before implementation, and the plan's step 1 re-checks this comment is still the newest ruling).

RULING 1 — decide_intent MINTS AND DOES NOT ACTIVATE. Measured: planning-services.ts:203-231 documents approval.decide as J1's approve-and-activate, "one click and one transaction" (design 299), with `activateInitialGraph` performing the single durable commit for both halves. Activation from a second command kind would be a competing activation authority to keep in lockstep forever. decide_intent's product purpose (the whole T1 chain) is the SERVER-DERIVED record — the record approval.decide takes from caller bytes today. So: this row commits the record and returns the authority verdict; NO graph/goal transition, NO activateInitialGraph call. Migrating approval.decide to CONSUME the minted record instead of its payload record is a named successor row, filed only after this lands.

RULING 2 — AGGREGATE, EVENT, AND THE TWO-RECORDS QUESTION. The mint writes ONE event to a SERVER-DERIVED per-run aggregate (id derived from projectId+runId with a namespace prefix, following the deriveActivationAggregateId bounded-namespace idiom), event type in the house style (e.g. "ApprovalIntentRecordMinted" — worker mirrors the neighboring planning event-type naming), committed through the existing decision seam with expectedVersion 0. THE FENCE IS THE SEMANTICS: exactly one server-derived record per run can ever exist; a second decide_intent for the same run refuses on the store fence with the mapped stable code (and the anti-bricking guard means its step-up burn must not have happened — see the plan's ordering). Relationship to approval.decide's payload record: DISJOINT SURFACES TODAY, by design — approval.decide remains the activation authority and its record path is untouched by this row; an arm pins that a decide_intent mint writes NOTHING to the aggregates approval.decide owns (no cross-write), so no consumer can read the two as one. Supersession/unification is the successor row's question, not a silent behavior here.

RULING 3 — THE TWO SOURCELESS FIELDS.
(a) `validity` = "CURRENT" AS A STRUCTURAL LIFECYCLE FACT, not a human choice. Measured: RUNTIME_LIFECYCLES.APPROVAL_VALIDITY = [CURRENT, INVALIDATED, SUPERSEDED]; the ONLY writers of the other two states are the post-hoc invalidation machinery (approval-invalidation.ts:129 SUPERSEDED, :134 INVALIDATED-vs-CURRENT), and the witness reader (planning-authority-reader-witness.ts:73) requires validity === "CURRENT" for a live decided record. A freshly DECIDED record is CURRENT by definition of the lifecycle, exactly as `lifecycle: "DECIDED"` is derivable. The mint pins the literal; an arm asserts no mint path can emit the other two members.
(b) `dependencyChanges` — THE PRODUCER IS THE HUMAN'S OWN PAYLOAD, MADE EXPLICIT. Measured: no durable producer exists anywhere (grep: only the core contract and a demo seed), and APPROVAL_INTENT_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [decision, decisionReason, runId] gives the human no way to express changes — so a server-side empty default would fabricate "the human approved zero dependency changes" without ever asking. But `decision` and `decisionReason` are ALREADY human-authored payload fields of the same HUMAN_APPROVED record; dependencyChanges is the same class of fact and gets the same source. RULING: widen APPROVAL_INTENT_PAYLOAD_KEYS to [decision, decisionReason, dependencyChanges, runId] (sorted, as the roster demands); the field is REQUIRED and validated to the exact shape {additions, challenges, removals} with ref-list members (core's validDependencyChanges is the shape authority — compose, don't re-declare); an EXPLICIT empty tuple is the human asserting "no dependency changes", which is an assertion, not a default; a payload missing the field or malformed refuses at the exact-shape ingress with the seam's existing code. Nothing is defaulted, nothing invented; the human's authority stays with the human. Fan-out of the roster widening (exact-key pins, senders) is enumerated at plan step 1 per rail E7(B).

ARCHITECT REPLAN MEASUREMENT (HEAD c39553412f3bdc87ea2ab1958e92b2e7868604d2; read-only; no source bytes authored).

The worker's three findings are confirmed and force BUILD-ORDER leaves rather than a wider main-row roster.

1. CORE ADMISSION. @moe/core exposes only the bare root; from apps/daemon applyApprovalCommand is reachable but validateApprovalRecord / validateApprovalDependencyChanges are not, and a deep import is blocked. An applyApprovalCommand-only ingress is rejected: it can validate dependencyChanges only after durable/state-hiding fences, so mapping its whole-record INPUT_INVALID to caller shape would misattribute the refusing layer. The safe hybrid is (a) a hostile-safe public validateApprovalDependencyChanges at readApprovalIntent, returning a detached snapshot and mapping undefined to APPROVAL_INTENT_SHAPE_INVALID @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT; (b) applyApprovalCommand later PRODUCES the frozen DECIDED record from a CURRENT/PENDING basis; (c) public validateApprovalRecord re-reads the durable event for DoD-3. Core index.ts is 434 lines, so publishing through the deliberately exclusive root first requires extracting its existing curated policy block to a <=250-line policy-public module; the root drops below 400. Exact root consumers are index-surface.test.ts (134->136 pins) and supersession-engine.test.ts (independent 134 count). A new package subpath is rejected because the core contract explicitly pins an exclusive root surface.

2. HUMAN PAYLOAD. Shape/sender reachability is exactly seven files: approval-intent-contracts.ts, approval-intent.ts/test, daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts, daemon-command-registry.test.ts, control-room v2/goals/plan-approval.ts and approve-plan.test.tsx. No generated client/digest rotates. The row consumes the public core partial validator, requires sorted [decision,decisionReason,dependencyChanges,runId], preserves the validator-returned snapshot, and updates the sole production sender. Missing/malformed nested bytes assert APPROVAL_INTENT_SHAPE_INVALID @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT; divergence fixture supplies all four top-level keys and otherwise-valid downstream state so the nested guard is the only refusing mechanism.

3. ATOMIC REPLAY LEG. observeReplayMarker currently commits independently. No burn-then-commit compensation can close the crash window. The identity leaf splits the 394-line session-authority-store.ts into <=250-line reader, decision, and replay-marker modules behind the compatible barrel, and makes buildReplayMarkerDecisionLeg the single authoritative producer consumed by observeReplayMarker. Main later commits record leg[0] + replay leg[1] in ONE commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs call. Divergence arms distinguish prefilled record only -> APPROVAL_INTENT_RECORD_CONFLICT @ DURABLE_STORE with marker untouched, from preburned replay only -> SESSION_REPLAYED @ REPLAY with record untouched.

Proposed dependency order: core-barrel extraction -> public approval validators -> payload widening -> this mint; atomic replay leaf independently -> this mint. The mint remains a six-path composition row. This is four production prerequisite rows, not evidence/security rows; each has a durable consumer edge. No existing epic row owns any measured capability or target path.
